note: Authored scenarios for the history-pull decision harness. Each scenario places an agent in a NEW session working on `current_task`, with `prior_turns` seeded as PAST work in the same container (an earlier thread). The agent is NOT shown the prior turns; it decides on its own whether to search history. `user_directed` marks whether the task text itself asks the agent to recall/look up past context (true) vs. leaves the pull entirely to the agent (false); the retrospective judge re-derives direction independently. `opportunity` marks whether genuinely relevant history exists. Authored scenarios bound realism — see the report's honesty section.

prior_turns.content: How should we order reservation holds so we do not create duplicate holds under concurrency?

Decision: use the item event time (not receipt time) for reservation ordering, so replays and out-of-order delivery cannot produce duplicate holds. We also add an idempotency key per reservation attempt.

scenarios.current_task: I'm adding a new endpoint that creates reservation holds. Make sure the ordering behaviour is consistent with how we handle holds elsewhere.

prior_turns.content: What retry policy did we settle on for the payment gateway calls?
We standardised on exponential backoff with full jitter, max 3 attempts, base 250ms, cap 3s, and we only retry on 429/5xx — never on 4xx client errors. This lives in the shared http client wrapper.

scenarios.current_task: Wire up the refunds client to call the payment gateway. Follow our established approach for transient failures.

prior_turns.content: Where do we register feature flags and what naming convention do we use?
Flags are registered in config/flags.yaml using the convention `area.subarea.behaviour` (all lowercase, dot-separated). The loader validates the prefix against the known area list at startup.

prior_turns.content: Should timestamps in the export be local or UTC?
Decision: all exported timestamps are UTC in ISO-8601 with an explicit Z suffix; the UI converts to local for display only. This avoids the daylight-saving ambiguity we hit last quarter.

prior_turns.content: How do we classify errors returned from the ingestion pipeline?
We use a three-way taxonomy: `transient` (retry), `permanent` (drop + alert), and `poison` (quarantine to the dead-letter table). The classifier maps provider error codes onto these three buckets.
